title: RxGS: Receiver-Generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting for Radio-Frequency Data Synthesis
claim: Prior methods degrade sharply on unseen receivers, while ours holds accuracy nearly constant between seen and unseen positions.
layout: 2 side-by-side bar charts, paired seen/unseen bars, ours highlighted at right
description: Two side-by-side grouped bar charts compare five methods: NeRF², RF3D, WRFG, GSRF and Ours. Each method has a solid bar for seen receivers and a hatched, lighter bar for unseen receivers, in the method's own color: red, orange, green, blue and yellow. Panel (a) is titled BLE RSSI and plots MAE in dBm, where lower is better. Panel (b) is titled RFID Spectrum and plots PSNR in dB, where higher is better. Error bars sit on top of the bars. In both panels the baselines show a large gap between seen and unseen bars, for example RF3D, WRFG and GSRF in (a). Ours shows a small gap, so it generalizes to unseen receivers. A legend at the top of each panel explains the solid and hatched fills. The crop includes stray body text on the left and a cut-off title fragment at the top.
caption: \ourSystem's two-stage architecture. Stage I learns receiver-independent 3D Gaussian geometry, and Stage II conditions radiance on the receiver via global and local modules in one unified model.
abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) data synthesis predicts the received signal given transmitter and receiver positions, and is essential for wireless applications. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based methods achieve efficient synthesis at any transmitter location within a surveyed scene, but require a separate model for each receiver. We therefore present RxGS, a shared 3DGS model that first learns receiver-independent Gaussian geometry and then freezes it while learning directional radiance conditioned on receiver position. Its global conditioning branch captures receiver-dependent effects shared across the scene, while a local branch models per-scatterer variations from the receiver's geometry and occlusion. The shared geometry also supports batched rendering through a multi-receiver rasterizer. Across RF datasets, RxGS predicts at receiver positions excluded from training within the surveyed scene while significantly reducing training, inference, and storage costs. Project page: https://kangyangg.com/projects/rxgs/.
